decks.name: D1 Quintorius Spirits
decks.notes: Lorehold spirit recursion. Fill the graveyard with cheap instants, sorceries and artifacts, then turn each one into a 3/2 Spirit and cast it again for free. The graveyard is the resource, not a byproduct.

strategy.strategy: Lorehold spirit recursion. Fill the graveyard with cheap instants, sorceries and artifacts, then turn each one into a 3/2 Spirit and cast it again for free. The graveyard is the resource, not a byproduct.
strategy.engine: Quintorius exiles a noncreature card from your graveyard each end step and makes a 3/2 Spirit; sacrifice a Spirit to cast that exiled card without paying its cost. 33 cards in the deck move cards out of the graveyard to keep the trigger fed, backed by 16 recursion pieces.
strategy.attack: Go wide with 3/2 Spirit tokens under anthem effects. Every removal spell they answer comes back, so the board rebuilds faster than opponents can clear it. Gandalf, Goblins' Bane converts the noncreature spell density into reach damage.
strategy.defense: Cheap instant-speed removal that doubles as graveyard fuel, Spirits as free chump blockers, and Deflecting Palm to turn a lethal swing back on its controller.
strategy.ramp: 10 pieces, weighted to 2-mana rocks and Equipment-based land fetch so the curve stays under 3. 38 lands, 9 nonbasic, none entering tapped.

decks.name: D2 Chulane Value Loop
decks.notes: Creature-flood value. Every creature spell draws a card and drops a land, so board, mana and hand all grow on the same trigger. The deck wins by simply doing more per turn than anyone else.

strategy.strategy: Creature-flood value. Every creature spell draws a card and drops a land, so board, mana and hand all grow on the same trigger. The deck wins by simply doing more per turn than anyone else.
strategy.engine: Chulane's cast trigger plus 45 enter-the-battlefield creatures and 7 blink or bounce effects (Ephemerate, Soulherder, Temur Sabertooth) to re-run them. Freed from the Real is the combo line with a mana-producing creature. Ancient Greenwarden doubles every land trigger.
strategy.attack: Widest creature count in the pod at 52. Zendikar's Roil turns Chulane's free land drops into 2/2 bodies, and the board outgrows blockers rather than evading them.
strategy.defense: 9 removal spells, a wall of enter-the-battlefield blockers, and Chulane's own bounce ability to rescue a creature and re-buy its trigger.
strategy.ramp: 11 dedicated pieces on top of Chulane's free land drops. 38 lands, 7 nonbasic, none entering tapped.

cards: Venat, Heart of Hydaelyn // Hydaelyn, the Mothercrystal

strategy.strategy: Proliferate control. Land a counter on anything that matters, then add to every counter on the board each end step until the accumulated advantage ends the game. The pod's control seat.
strategy.engine: Atraxa's end-step proliferate with 18 proliferate sources and 18 counter payoffs: Ichormoon Gauntlet, Innkeeper's Talent, Branching Evolution, Inexorable Tide, Flux Channeler, Karn's Bastion and Viral Drake.
strategy.attack: Atraxa herself is a 4/4 flying deathtouch lifelink clock. Viral Drake converts proliferate into poison counters as a second, faster win route while +1/+1 counter creatures grow past blockers.
strategy.defense: Heaviest interaction in the pod at 10 removal including sweepers, plus lifelink on the commander to buy turns against aggression.
strategy.ramp: 10 pieces weighted toward four-colour fixing rather than raw acceleration. 37 lands, 7 nonbasic, none entering tapped.

decks.notes: Toughness fortress. Creatures deal combat damage equal to toughness and ignore defender, so the same permanents that hold the ground are the offense. Nothing in the deck is a dead card on either side of the table.
cards: Venat, Heart of Hydaelyn // Hydaelyn, the Mothercrystal

strategy.strategy: Toughness fortress. Creatures deal combat damage equal to toughness and ignore defender, so the same permanents that hold the ground are the offense. Nothing in the deck is a dead card on either side of the table.
strategy.engine: Felothar's static rewrite over 20 defenders and 22 high-toughness bodies. His sacrifice ability turns a fat blocker into a fistful of cards. Canopy Gargantuan adds counters equal to each creature's toughness every upkeep, compounding both halves at once.
strategy.attack: Walls swing for their toughness, which is where the deck's stats actually live. Damage scales with the same numbers that make the board hard to attack into.
strategy.defense: The board is the defense: 20 defenders, 14 lifegain pieces and protection spells. The strongest ground defense of the seven.
strategy.ramp: 11 pieces, several of them defender-ramp creatures that block and produce mana in the same slot. 38 lands, 7 nonbasic, none entering tapped. 48 total mana sources, most in the pod.

strategy.strategy: Goblin go-wide. Krenko doubles the board every activation, then a damage payoff converts bodies into a win without needing combat to connect. The fastest clock in the pod.
strategy.engine: Krenko's tap ability with Thousand-Year Elixir and Thornbite Staff to untap him, so the token count squares instead of doubling. Purphoros turns every token that enters into 2 damage per opponent, which makes the engine lethal without attacking.

strategy.defense: Thinnest defense of the seven by design. Goblin Bombardment as the sacrifice outlet and reach, Swiftfoot Boots protecting Krenko, and raw speed as the answer to slower decks.
strategy.ramp: 9 pieces, mostly 2-mana rocks and rituals to deploy Krenko a turn early. 37 lands, 7 nonbasic, none entering tapped.
